supporting_observations.claim: At 13:40:12–13:40:15, WS-JFROST-01 obtained Kerberos tickets for ali.hassan to WS-AHASSAN-01, and WS-AHASSAN-01 recorded a network logon for ali.hassan originating from WS-JFROST-01. This is an unusual direction for the stated remote-administration practice, which is from WS-AHASSAN-01.
At 13:40:48, WS-JFROST-01 recorded a network logon for ali.hassan originating from WS-AHASSAN-01, shortly before the PowerShell process appeared on WS-JFROST-01.

At 13:42:53, PowerShell ran on WS-JFROST-01 as ali.hassan with the command to run \\FILE-MAP-01\IT\Patch-Workstations.ps1 using -NoProfile and -ExecutionPolicy Bypass. This matches the documented IT patching method, and the subsequent activity includes a Windows update download and wusa installing an MSU package.

Explorer wrote UserAssist values whose encoded path corresponds to the PowerShell executable at 13:32:27 and 14:12:59. These records do not show the command line or establish that either update corresponds to the reported window around 13:40.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records show the admin PowerShell process beginning at 13:42:53, not at the reported approximate time of 13:40; they do not establish whether that process caused the reported window.
The UserAssist records show registry value writes for a PowerShell path, not the associated process command lines or a precise execution time.
The evidence does not include the contents or integrity validation of Patch-Workstations.ps1, PowerShell transcripts, or an administrator confirmation of the session.
claims_not_established: Whether ali.hassan initiated or authorized the network logon from WS-JFROST-01 to WS-AHASSAN-01.
Whether the PowerShell window Julia observed was the documented patch script run, or a separate PowerShell execution.
Whether any PowerShell execution associated with the UserAssist entries performed unauthorized actions.
additional_evidence_needed: Confirm with ali.hassan whether they initiated the 13:40 activity and whether the WS-JFROST-01-to-WS-AHASSAN-01 logon was expected.
Collect PowerShell operational logs or transcripts, WinRM/WMI and remote-session logs, and the patch script contents and hash for the relevant run.
Obtain endpoint process-creation and UserAssist details sufficient to identify any Julia-launched PowerShell process and its command line around 13:40.
unrelated_findings: WS-JFROST-01 recorded a Kerberos logon for greta.lund from that workstation to WS-GLUND-01; this is outside the specific PowerShell alert assessment and should be reviewed separately. (T174-00034, T174-00036, T174-00038)
